posts.title: "In lieu of points": how to elect a defensive driving course at a North Dakota court so the points never post
posts.description: For a violation worth five points or fewer, North Dakota lets you choose an approved course instead of points, at the moment you post bond. Here is how the election works, what it costs, and the 30-day deadline.

faq.q: Does electing a course in lieu of points get my ticket dismissed?
faq.a: No. You still post the bond and it is still forfeited. What changes is that the points for the violation are never entered on your record.

faq.q: Which violations qualify for the in-lieu election?
faq.a: Violations carrying five points or fewer. Six-point-or-higher offenses and the excluded offenses under NDCC 39-06.1-05 (such as DUI, reckless driving, leaving the scene and driving under suspension) do not qualify.

faq.q: How often can I use it?
faq.a: Once every twelve months, and using it forfeits the three-point reduction option for that year.

posts.content:
**Short answer:** If you are cited in North Dakota for a violation worth five points or fewer, you can tell the court, at the time you post bond, that you elect to take an approved defensive driving course instead of having the points entered. The bond is still forfeited, but the points never reach your record. You then have 30 days to get proof of completion to NDDOT. You can do this once every twelve months, and doing it means you cannot also use the three-point reduction that year.

## Where this comes from

North Dakota Century Code 39-06.1-10.1 creates the election. It sits alongside the better-known three-point reduction in 39-06.1-13, and the two are alternatives, not a package.

## Who qualifies

- The violation must carry **five points or fewer** under the schedule in 39-06.1-10. Most speeding, stop-sign, signal and lane violations qualify.
- It must not be one of the **excluded offenses** in 39-06.1-05: driving under the influence, reckless driving, leaving the scene, driving under suspension or revocation, and similar.
- You must not have used the election in the **past twelve months**.

## How to make the election

1. **At the time you post bond**, tell the court clerk you elect to complete an approved course in lieu of points under 39-06.1-10.1. The election has to be made then, not later.
2. **Enroll in an approved course** the same day. NDDOT keeps the list of approved providers on its website. [Ours](/north-dakota) is four hours and $24.99.
3. **Finish the course** and download your certificate.
4. **Deliver proof of completion to NDDOT within 30 days** of the election, by email to drs@nd.gov or by mail to the Driver License Division in Bismarck. Miss the 30 days and the points are entered.

## What you give up

Two things. The bond is forfeited, so the money is gone either way. And you forfeit the three-point reduction under 39-06.1-13 for that twelve-month period. If you already have several points on your record, it is worth doing the arithmetic: keeping five new points off is usually better than taking three old ones off, but not always.

## What it is not

It is not a dismissal. The violation still happened and the bond is still forfeited. It is a way to keep the points, and their effect on your suspension math and your insurer's view of you, off the record.

## The arithmetic that matters

North Dakota suspends a license at twelve points, seven days for each point over eleven. A driver under 18 loses the license at six. If a new five-point violation would push you over either line, the in-lieu election is the difference between a course and a suspension.

posts.title: How North Dakota points, suspensions and the three-point reduction work in 2026
posts.description: Twelve points suspends a North Dakota license, seven days for every point over eleven. An approved course takes three off once a year. Here is the whole system in one place, with the statute.

faq.q: How many points suspends a North Dakota license?
faq.a: Twelve or more. The suspension is seven days for each point over eleven. A driver under 18 has the license canceled at six points.

faq.q: How many points does an approved course remove?
faq.a: Three, once every twelve months, up to nine points in any three-year period, and only points that were on the record before the course was completed.

faq.q: Can I take the course if I am already suspended?
faq.a: Yes, but the reduction applies only after the suspension is served.

posts.content:
**Short answer:** North Dakota assigns points to moving violations under NDCC 39-06.1-10. At twelve points your license is suspended, seven days for every point over eleven. Completing an approved defensive driving course reduces your points by three, once every twelve months, up to nine points in any three-year period. If you are already at twelve, the reduction applies after the suspension is served.

## How points accumulate

Each moving violation carries a point value fixed by statute. Common examples: most speeding violations carry one to five points depending on how far over the limit; failure to yield, stop-sign and signal violations sit in the same range; driving under the influence, reckless driving and leaving the scene carry more and are excluded from the in-lieu election. Points stay on the record and count toward the suspension threshold.

## The suspension line

- **Adults:** twelve or more points means a suspension of **seven days for every point over eleven**. Thirteen points is fourteen days; fifteen points is twenty-eight.
- **Under 18:** the license is **canceled at six points**.

## The three-point reduction

NDCC 39-06.1-13(2) lets the director reduce your accumulated points by three when you complete an approved course. Four rules:

1. **Once every twelve months.**
2. **No more than nine points in any three-year period**, measured from the date the last points were entered.
3. **Only points already on the record** when you finish the course. Points added afterwards are not touched.
4. **After a suspension is served**, if you were at twelve or more (or six or more as a minor) when you took the course.

The course is four hours. [Ours](/north-dakota) is $24.99, and the certificate is emailed the moment you pass.

## The other option: in lieu of points

If you have just been cited for a violation worth five points or fewer, you can elect at court to take the course instead of having the points entered at all. That is a different mechanism, with a 30-day submission deadline, and using it forfeits the reduction for that year. We wrote it up separately: [how the in-lieu election works](/north-dakota/blog/in-lieu-of-points-north-dakota-court-election).

## How NDDOT finds out

It does not, unless you tell it. North Dakota has no provider reporting system. You send your certificate to drs@nd.gov or mail it to the Driver License Division, and NDDOT applies the reduction. Keep a copy.

## What to do today

1. Request your driving record from NDDOT so you know your current total.
2. If a new ticket is pending and worth five points or fewer, ask the court about the in-lieu election before you post bond.
3. Otherwise, take an approved course and send NDDOT the certificate. Three points off, once a year, is the cheapest margin you can buy.
